title: Workflow opus5.5
author: nonsalantan
selftext:
Can someone explain how the workflow works with Opus 5.5? Do I simply describe what I want using prompts, and then it generates the code and scripts that I copy and paste into my game?

How do I create graphics and implement physics using Opus? 

Could someone walk me through the entire workflow, from describing my ideas to actually building a playable game?  
I’d really appreciate a clear, step-by-step explanation of how the whole process works.

comments.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
comments.body: Why copy? I don't even open my editor any more.

replies.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
replies.body: I use Unity, I just have to tell Claude the path to my project and what I want done. It will edit the C# files directly. If you connect an CLI/MCP it can also edit your Unity scenes (ask Claude how to set it up).

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: Same here. With Godot. I have it building an engine using Godot (yes, an engine to build an engine). I've only opened the editor once and then realized it was pointless to do so because Claude did literally everything via code.

comments.author: PhantomZenithOrigin
comments.body:
I think the minimum bar to entry here is posing this question to your AI.

What, are you afraid to burning tokens on simple questions like this?

replies.author: nonsalantan
replies.body: no i dont know how to use it right way

replies.author: UncleJoesLandscaping
replies.body: He is right though. If you ask claude "how do you develop games with opus5.5?" you will get the right answer.

replies.author: Recoil42
replies.body: FYI: Everyone telling you to ask your AI is right. Ask your AI. That's the whole secret. Do that, over and over. That's how you'll learn.

comments.author: Bitter_Cellist586
comments.body:
depends what you're building.  If it's a web app, you tell it that's what you want and you start describing it.  If it's a native iOS or Android app, it's often better to create a blank app template with Xcode or Android Studio, then use Claude to build on it. 

New users might not know they should add the project folder to the chat so AI knows where to put the files and artifacts.   

Claude can't natively create images so I often give it a Gemini API key so it can make them.

Claude can do physics quite well.  Good luck, if you're confused, definitely ask AI.
